references.text: Describes the sound of the trumpet on the Day of Atonement that inaugurates the Jubilee year mentioned in verse 10
Repeats the principle of returning to one's property in the Jubilee year
Elaborates on the law that sold property must be returned to its original owner in the Jubilee year
Concerns the release of Hebrew servants in the Jubilee year, which is part of the proclamation of liberty
Confirms that even those who have not been redeemed shall go free in the Jubilee year
Refers to the Jubilee year when land must return to its original owner
Mentions the Jubilee year in connection with inheritance rights and tribal property
Isaiah prophesies about proclaiming liberty for captives and a year of favor from the Lord, linking to the Jubilee's proclamation of liberty
Uses the expression 'proclaim liberty' (דְּרוֹר) in connection with the release of slaves
Refers to proclaiming liberty in the house of the Lord, using the same terminology as the Jubilee year
Ezekiel mentions the year of release (the Jubilee year) in connection with the prince and his property
Jesus reads from Isaiah 61 in the synagogue and declares the fulfillment of the spiritual meaning of the Jubilee year—liberty for captives and the Lord's year of favor
